compare_blocks.body:
Two colleagues might speak equally little during a lab meeting and both prefer time to think before responding. Their roles, familiarity with the topic and the meeting format can explain that similarity. How much either person speaks is a poor guide to Sensing or Intuition.

The shared letters describe three preferences. Introversion directs attention and energy toward the inner world of ideas and reflection. Thinking gives more weight to logical consistency and criteria that can be applied across cases. Perceiving describes a preference for keeping options open and taking in new information when dealing with the outside world.

(Fictional scene) A colleague's published result will not reproduce, twenty per cent off. (Fictional example) A colleague is taking over the analysis scripts. Both people have the same code, dataset and environment. One way to help is to explain how the modules fit together so the colleague can adapt the script. Another is to demonstrate a complete run so they can see the inputs, outputs and settings. Either type can teach both ways.

(Fictional example) At 8 p.m., a video call drops and the router light turns orange. A pattern-based approach asks whether several devices or neighbours lose service at the same times. The light alone cannot distinguish a provider issue from a local problem.

Reports from neighbours can suggest a wider problem. Comparing affected devices can narrow down a local issue. Both findings are clues that can guide the next check. Neither shows what type the person troubleshooting is.

Log the time, duration and device affected. That gives the provider concrete information to work with when you report the problem.

Two colleagues might speak equally little during a lab meeting and both prefer time to think before responding. Their roles, familiarity with the topic and the meeting format can explain that similarity. How much either person speaks is a poor guide to Sensing or Intuition.

Thinking gives more weight to logical consistency and criteria that can be applied across cases. Perceiving describes a preference for keeping options open and taking in new information when dealing with the outside world.

(Fictional scene) A colleague's published result will not reproduce, twenty per cent off. sections.title: Quick answer

sections.body_md:
Two colleagues might speak equally little during a lab meeting and both prefer time to think before responding. Their roles, familiarity with the topic and the meeting format can explain that similarity. How much either person speaks is a poor guide to Sensing or Intuition.

The shared letters describe three preferences. Introversion directs attention and energy toward the inner world of ideas and reflection. Thinking gives more weight to logical consistency and criteria that can be applied across cases. Perceiving describes a preference for keeping options open and taking in new information when dealing with the outside world.

The Sensing–Intuition distinction is about the information someone tends to trust or notice: concrete observations and experience, or connections, patterns and possibilities. A careful conclusion can draw on both.

### INTP and ISTP: what each approach notices when the data disagree

A mismatch in the same dataset can raise questions about how the measurements fit together or how they were produced. In this fictional example, an Intuition-oriented reading looks for a pattern across samples and asks whether it fits the model. A Sensing-oriented reading checks what was logged about the probe, supplies and calibration. Either person could investigate both.

Looking for a pattern might reveal that two variables were treated as one. Checking the setup might uncover a loose connection. Pursuing only one explanation can delay the other check, so both hypotheses need evidence.

Either person might recall a similar shift in earlier readings or question the proposed mechanism. What they investigate depends on their responsibilities, familiarity with the equipment, deadline and access to records. A single response cannot establish type.

### INTP and ISTP: why they share Ti and Fe but differ in Ne and Se

In type dynamics, both codes have I and P. For an introverted type with P, the perceiving process faces outward and supports the inward-facing judging process. With T shared, both have dominant Ti. Changing N to S changes the outward-facing auxiliary from Ne to Se, while Fe stays in the inferior position.

INTP’s auxiliary Ne explores outward connections and possibilities. ISTP’s auxiliary Se attends to what is observable in the immediate environment. In the convention used here, INTP’s tertiary Si draws on remembered experience, and ISTP’s tertiary Ni looks for an underlying pattern. These are descriptions within the model. They cannot establish what someone will do first or how well they will do it.

The Foundation’s overview allows either attitude for the tertiary process: Sensing can be written as Se or Si for INTP, and Intuition as Ne or Ni for ISTP. This page uses Si and Ni. The dominant and auxiliary processes stay the same across those conventions. See the [INTP profile](/en/personality/intp) and the [ISTP profile](/en/personality/istp).

| Same task and conditions | INTP: patterns and possibilities | ISTP: observations and experience | What the row illustrates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

sections.body_md:
These four fictional examples illustrate different ways of gathering information. They do not show who can run an experiment, who should take a job or how to identify either type.

Start with two colleagues in the same lab, working from the same set of inconsistent measurements.

### INTP and ISTP: a replication fails, and which end to work back from

(Fictional scene) A colleague's published result will not reproduce, twenty per cent off. With the same method and the same rig in front of them, one approach re-derives the colleague's model to see whether a premise was assumed away without being stated; the other walks the written steps again and checks whether the actual state at each step matches the description. Under the same conditions, INTP and ISTP can both take either approach.

Re-deriving the model can uncover an unstated assumption, but the paper might omit a detail needed to test it. Checking the procedure can surface a difference in the setup, provided the written method is clear enough to compare. The colleagues could time-box both checks and compare what they found before choosing an explanation.

Record what was known, who was responsible for each part, what the procedure required and which evidence changed the conclusion. That helps explain the decision without assigning a type.

### INTP and ISTP: teaching a colleague to rerun your code

(Fictional example) A colleague is taking over the analysis scripts. Both people have the same code, dataset and environment. One way to help is to explain how the modules fit together so the colleague can adapt the script. Another is to demonstrate a complete run so they can see the inputs, outputs and settings. Either type can teach both ways.

A walkthrough can get the colleague to a working result, while a discussion of the design can help them adapt the code later. Choose based on what they need to do on their own, how much time they have and whether the environment is working. Teaching style cannot distinguish INTP from ISTP.

### INTP and ISTP: whether the outlier goes into the report

(Fictional example) One reading remains unusual after repeat measurement. One question is whether the reading fits a plausible mechanism. Another is whether the records document a change in the measurement procedure. Either type can ask both. The study’s prespecified rules govern how to handle and report the outlier.

A proposed explanation belongs in the report as a hypothesis until evidence supports it. An additional control may help if the outlier could change the result and the study permits the check. If the team cannot verify the cause, report that limitation and how it might affect the conclusion.

### INTP and ISTP: the shared flat where the network keeps dropping

(Fictional example) At 8 p.m., a video call drops and the router light turns orange. A pattern-based approach asks whether several devices or neighbours lose service at the same times. An observation-based approach compares which devices are affected and what the router indicates when the connection drops. Either type can do both. The light alone cannot distinguish a provider issue from a local problem.

Reports from neighbours can suggest a wider problem. Comparing affected devices can narrow down a local issue. Both findings are clues that can guide the next check. Neither shows what type the person troubleshooting is.

Log the time, duration and device affected. That gives the provider concrete information to work with when you report the problem.
